segs.e: Heartfelt Sayings 1.1
Upon Awakening (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the tree of awakening on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sattāhaṁ ekapallaṅkena nisinno hoti vimuttisukhapaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: There the Buddha sat cross-legged for seven days without moving, experiencing the bliss of freedom.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā rattiyā paṭhamaṁ yāmaṁ paṭiccasamuppādaṁ anulomaṁ sādhukaṁ manasākāsi:
segs.e: When seven days had passed, the Buddha emerged from that state of immersion. In the first part of the night, he carefully applied the mind to dependent origination, going with the grain:

segs.p: “Iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: “So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“When things become clear
to the keen, meditating brahmin,
his doubts are dispelled,
since he understands each thing and its cause.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.2
Upon Awakening (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the tree of awakening on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sattāhaṁ ekapallaṅkena nisinno hoti vimuttisukhapaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: There the Buddha sat cross-legged for seven days without moving, experiencing the bliss of freedom.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā rattiyā majjhimaṁ yāmaṁ paṭiccasamuppādaṁ paṭilomaṁ sādhukaṁ manasākāsi:
segs.e: When seven days had passed, the Buddha emerged from that state of immersion. In the second part of the night, he carefully applied the mind to dependent origination, going against the grain:

segs.p: “Iti imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: “So, when this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
When ignorance ceases, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases.
When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.
When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases.
When contact ceases, feeling ceases.
When feeling ceases, craving ceases.
When craving ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“When things become clear
to the keen, meditating brahmin,
his doubts are dispelled,
since he’s known the end of conditions.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.3
Upon Awakening (3rd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the tree of awakening on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sattāhaṁ ekapallaṅkena nisinno hoti vimuttisukhapaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: There the Buddha sat cross-legged for seven days without moving, experiencing the bliss of freedom.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā rattiyā pacchimaṁ yāmaṁ paṭiccasamuppādaṁ anulomapaṭilomaṁ sādhukaṁ manasākāsi:
segs.e: When seven days had passed, the Buddha emerged from that state of immersion. In the last watch, he carefully applied the mind to dependent origination, going both with and against the grain:

segs.p: “Iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati,
segs.e: “So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati; yadidaṁ—
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases.
When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.
When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases.
When contact ceases, feeling ceases.
When feeling ceases, craving ceases.
When craving ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“When things become clear
to the keen, meditating brahmin,
he remains, scattering Māra’s army,
as the sun lights up the sky.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.4
The Mystic Syllable Huṁ
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sattāhaṁ ekapallaṅkena nisinno hoti vimuttisukhapaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: There the Buddha sat cross-legged for seven days without moving, experiencing the bliss of freedom.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: When seven days had passed, the Buddha emerged from that state of immersion.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro huṁhuṅkajātiko brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin, one of those who murmured the mystic syllable huṁ, huṁ, went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he stood to one side and said,

segs.p: “kittāvatā nu kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo hoti, katame ca pana brāhmaṇakaraṇā dhammā”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, how do you define a brahmin? And what are the things that make one a brahmin?”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Any brahmin who has banished bad qualities—
not murmuring the mystic syllable huṁ, unstained, self-controlled,
a complete knowledge master <j>who has completed the spiritual journey—
they may legitimately proclaim the divine doctrine;
who have no pretensions about anything in the world.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.5
The Brahmin
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca mahākaccāno āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmā ca mahākappino āyasmā ca mahācundo āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca revato āyasmā ca nando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu.
segs.e: Now at that time a number of senior monks approached the Buddha—the venerables Sāriputta, Mahāmoggallāna, Mahākassapa, Mahākaccāna, Mahākoṭṭhita, Mahākappina, Mahācunda, Anuruddha, Revata, and Nanda.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā te āyasmante dūratova āgacchante;
segs.e: The Buddha saw them coming off in the distance,
and addressed the mendicants:
“These, mendicants, are brahmins coming!
These are brahmins coming!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro brāhmaṇajātiko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, a certain mendicant who was brahmin by birth asked the Buddha,

segs.p: “kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, brāhmaṇo hoti, katame ca pana brāhmaṇakaraṇā dhammā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how do you define a brahmin? And what are the things that make one a brahmin?”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Having banished bad qualities,
those who live always mindful,
with fetters ended, awakened,
they are the world’s true brahmins.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.6
With Mahākassapa
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākassapo pippaliguhāyaṁ viharati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Mahākassapa was staying in the Pipphali cave, and he was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo aparena samayena tamhā ābādhā vuṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then after some time he recovered from that illness.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato mahākassapassa tamhā ābādhā vuṭṭhitassa etadahosi:
segs.e: It occurred to him,
“Why not enter Rājagaha for almsfood?”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena pañcamattāni devatāsatāni ussukkaṁ āpannāni honti āyasmato mahākassapassa piṇḍapātapaṭilābhāya.
segs.e: Now at that time five hundred deities were ready and eager for the chance to offer alms to Mahākassapa.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo tāni pañcamattāni devatāsatāni paṭikkhipitvā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi—
segs.e: But Mahākasspa turned down those deities. In the morning, he robed up, took his bowl and robe, and entered Rājagaha for alms.
He went to the street markets of the poor, the destitute, and the embroiderers.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ rājagahe piṇḍāya carantaṁ yena daliddavisikhā kapaṇavisikhā pesakāravisikhā.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him wandering for alms in the street markets of the poor, the destitute, and the embroiderers.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“The stranger, providing for no other,
tamed, consolidated in the core,
with defilements ended and flaws purged:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.7
At Ajakalāpaka
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā pāvāyaṁ viharati ajakalāpake cetiye, ajakalāpakassa yakkhassa bhavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in Pāvā at the Ajakalāpaka Shrine, the haunt of the native spirit Ajakalāpaka.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ abbhokāse nisinno hoti; devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

segs.p: Atha kho ajakalāpako yakkho bhagavato bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁsaṁ uppādetukāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato avidūre tikkhattuṁ “akkulo pakkulo”ti akkulapakkulikaṁ akāsi:
segs.e: Then Ajakalāpaka, wanting to make the Buddha feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, approached him, and while not far away yelled three times, “Havoc and heck!” Then he added,
“Now that’s a goblin for you, ascetic!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“When a brahmin gets over
their own issues,
they transcend this goblin
and his havoc.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.8
With Saṅgāmaji
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā saṅgāmaji sāvatthiṁ anuppatto hoti bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Saṅgāmaji had arrived at Sāvatthī to see the Buddha.
His former wife heard
that he had arrived,
and went to the Jetavana, taking their boy.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā saṅgāmaji aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṁ nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Saṅgāmaji was sitting at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purāṇadutiyikā yenāyasmā saṅgāmaji tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ saṅgāmajiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then his former wife went up to him and said,
“Ascetic, please raise this little boy.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā saṅgāmaji tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: When she said this, Saṅgāmaji kept silent.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purāṇadutiyikā āyasmantaṁ saṅgāmajiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time she said,
“Ascetic, please raise this little boy.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā saṅgāmaji tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: For a second time, Saṅgāmaji kept silent.

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purāṇadutiyikā āyasmantaṁ saṅgāmajiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time she said,
“Ascetic, please raise this little boy.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā saṅgāmaji tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: For a third time, Saṅgāmaji kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purāṇadutiyikā taṁ dārakaṁ āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purato nikkhipitvā pakkāmi:
segs.e: Then she put down the boy in front of Saṅgāmaji, saying,
“This is your child, ascetic. Please raise him.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā saṅgāmaji taṁ dārakaṁ neva olokesi nāpi ālapi.
segs.e: But Saṅgāmaji neither looked at the boy nor spoke to him.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purāṇadutiyikā avidūraṁ gantvā apalokentī addasa āyasmantaṁ saṅgāmajiṁ taṁ dārakaṁ neva olokentaṁ nāpi ālapantaṁ, disvānassā etadahosi:
segs.e: Then his former wife went a little distance away. Looking back, she saw Saṅgāmaji ignoring the boy, and thought,
“This ascetic doesn’t even want his child.”
She returned to pick up the boy, then left.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena āyasmato saṅgāmajissa purāṇadutiyikāya evarūpaṁ vippakāraṁ.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, the Buddha saw how Saṅgāmaji’s former wife went back for the child.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“When she came he was not glad,
when she left he did not grieve.
Victorious in battle, freed from chains,
that’s who I declare a brahmin.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.9
Matted Hair Ascetics
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā gayāyaṁ viharati gayāsīse.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Gayā on Gayā Head.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā jaṭilā sītāsu hemantikāsu rattīsu antaraṭṭhake himapātasamaye gayāyaṁ ummujjantipi nimujjantipi, ummujjanimujjampi karonti osiñcantipi, aggimpi juhanti:
segs.e: Now at that time—during the cold spell when the snow falls in the January winter—many matted hair ascetics plunged in and out of the Gayā river. Plunging and showering, they served the sacred flame, thinking:
“Through this there is purity.”

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā te sambahule jaṭile sītāsu hemantikāsu rattīsu antaraṭṭhake himapātasamaye gayāyaṁ ummujjantepi nimujjantepi ummujjanimujjampi karonte osiñcantepi aggimpi juhante:
segs.e: The Buddha saw them plunging in and out.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Purity doesn’t come from water,
no matter how many people bathe there.
One who has truth and principle,
they are pure, they are brahmins.”
Heartfelt Sayings 1.10
With Bāhiya
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bāhiyo dārucīriyo suppārake paṭivasati samuddatīre sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time Bāhiya of the Bark Cloth was residing by Suppāraka on the ocean shore, where he was honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And he received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Atha kho bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

segs.p: “ye kho keci loke arahanto vā arahattamaggaṁ vā samāpannā, ahaṁ tesaṁ aññataro”ti.
segs.e: “I am one of those in the world who are perfected or on the path to perfection.”

segs.p: Atha kho bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa purāṇasālohitā devatā anukampikā atthakāmā bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bāhiyo dārucīriyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bāhiyaṁ dārucīriyaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a deity who was a former relative of Bāhiya, having sympathy and wanting what’s best for him, approached him and said:

segs.p: “neva kho tvaṁ, bāhiya, arahā, nāpi arahattamaggaṁ vā samāpanno.
segs.e: “Bāhiya, you’re not a perfected one, nor on the path to perfection.

segs.p: Sāpi te paṭipadā natthi yāya tvaṁ arahā vā assa arahattamaggaṁ vā samāpanno”ti.
segs.e: You don’t have the practice by which you might become a perfected one or one on the path to perfection.”

segs.p: “Atha ke carahi sadevake loke arahanto vā arahattamaggaṁ vā samāpannā”ti?
segs.e: “So who then are those in the world who are perfected or on the path to perfection?”

segs.p: “Atthi, bāhiya, uttaresu janapadesu sāvatthī nāma nagaraṁ.
segs.e: “In the northern lands there is a city named Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tattha so bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.
segs.e: There that Blessed One is now staying, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: So hi, bāhiya, bhagavā arahā ceva arahattāya ca dhammaṁ desetī”ti.
segs.e: He is a perfected one and teaches the Dhamma for the sake of perfection.”

segs.p: Atha kho bāhiyo dārucīriyo tāya devatāya saṁvejito tāvadeva suppārakamhā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Impelled by that deity, Bāhiya left Suppāraka right away.

segs.p: Sabbattha ekarattiparivāsena yena sāvatthī jetavanaṁ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Sojourning no more than a single night in any place, he made his way to Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery in the Jeta Grove at Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū abbhokāse caṅkamanti.
segs.e: At that time several mendicants were walking mindfully in the open air.

segs.p: Atha kho bāhiyo dārucīriyo yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: Bāhiya approached them and said,

segs.p: “kahaṁ nu kho, bhante, etarahi bhagavā viharati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho?
segs.e: “Sirs, where is the Blessed One at present, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha?

segs.p: Dassanakāmamhā mayaṁ taṁ bhagavantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhan”ti.
segs.e: For I want to see him.”
“He has entered an inhabited area for almsfood, Bāhiya.”

segs.p: Atha kho bāhiyo dārucīriyo taramānarūpo jetavanā nikkhamitvā sāvatthiṁ pavisitvā addasa bhagavantaṁ sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya carantaṁ pāsādikaṁ pasādanīyaṁ santindriyaṁ santamānasaṁ uttamadamathasamathamanuppattaṁ dantaṁ guttaṁ yatindriyaṁ nāgaṁ.
segs.e: Then Bāhiya rushed out of the Jeta Grove and entered Sāvatthī, where he saw the Buddha walking for alms. He was impressive and inspiring, with peaceful faculties and heart, attained to the highest self-control and serenity, like an elephant with tamed, guarded, and controlled faculties.

segs.p: Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pāde sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Bāhiya went up to the Buddha, bowed down with his head to the Buddha’s feet, and said,

segs.p: “desetu me, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṁ; desetu sugato dhammaṁ,
segs.e: “Sir, let the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma! Let the Holy One teach me the Dhamma!
That would be for my lasting welfare and happiness.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā bāhiyaṁ dārucīriyaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “akālo kho tāva, bāhiya, antaragharaṁ paviṭṭhamhā piṇḍāyā”ti.
segs.e: “It’s not the time, Bāhiya, so long as I have entered an inhabited area for almsfood.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bāhiyo dārucīriyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, Bāhiya said,

segs.p: “dujjānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhante, bhagavato vā jīvitantarāyānaṁ, mayhaṁ vā jīvitantarāyānaṁ.
segs.e: “But you never know, sir, when life is at risk, either the Buddha’s or my own.
Let the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma! Let the Holy One teach me the Dhamma!

segs.p: desetu sugato dhammaṁ, yaṁ mamassa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: That would be for my lasting welfare and happiness.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā bāhiyaṁ dārucīriyaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, the Buddha said,

segs.p: “akālo kho tāva, bāhiya, antaragharaṁ paviṭṭhamhā piṇḍāyā”ti.
segs.e: “It’s not the time, Bāhiya, so long as I have entered an inhabited area for almsfood.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho bāhiyo dārucīriyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, Bāhiya said,

segs.p: “dujjānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhante, bhagavato vā jīvitantarāyānaṁ, mayhaṁ vā jīvitantarāyānaṁ.
segs.e: “But you never know, sir, when life is at risk, either the Buddha’s or my own.
Let the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma! Let the Holy One teach me the Dhamma!

segs.p: desetu sugato dhammaṁ, yaṁ mamassa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: That would be for my lasting welfare and happiness.”
“In that case, Bāhiya, you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṁ bhavissati, sute sutamattaṁ bhavissati, mute mutamattaṁ bhavissati, viññāte viññātamattaṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘In the seen will be merely the seen; in the heard will be merely the heard; in the thought will be merely the thought; in the known will be merely the known.’
That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Yato kho te, bāhiya, diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṁ bhavissati, sute sutamattaṁ bhavissati, mute mutamattaṁ bhavissati, viññāte viññātamattaṁ bhavissati,
segs.e: When you have trained in this way,
you won’t be ‘by that’.
When you’re not ‘by that’,
you won’t be ‘in that’.
When you’re not ‘in that’,

segs.p: tato tvaṁ, bāhiya, nevidha na huraṁ na ubhayamantarena.
segs.e: you won’t be in this life or the next or between the two.
Just this is the end of suffering.”

segs.p: Atha kho bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa bhagavato imāya saṅkhittāya dhammadesanāya tāvadeva anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucci.
segs.e: Then, due to this brief Dhamma teaching of the Buddha, Bāhiya’s mind was right away freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā bāhiyaṁ dārucīriyaṁ iminā saṅkhittena ovādena ovaditvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: And when the Buddha had given Bāhiya this brief advice he left.

segs.p: Atha kho acirapakkantassa bhagavato bāhiyaṁ dārucīriyaṁ gāvī taruṇavacchā adhipatitvā jīvitā voropesi.
segs.e: But soon after the Buddha had left, a cow with a baby calf charged at Bāhiya and took his life.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ nagaramhā nikkhamitvā addasa bāhiyaṁ dārucīriyaṁ kālaṅkataṁ;
segs.e: Then the Buddha wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he exited the city together with several mendicants and saw that Bāhiya had passed away.
He said to the monks,

segs.p: “gaṇhatha, bhikkhave, bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa sarīrakaṁ; mañcakaṁ āropetvā nīharitvā jhāpetha; thūpañcassa karotha.
segs.e: “Mendicants, pick up Bāhiya’s corpse. Having lifted it onto a cot and carried it, cremate it and build a monument.
Mendicants, one of your spiritual companions has passed away.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa sarīrakaṁ mañcakaṁ āropetvā nīharitvā jhāpetvā thūpañcassa katvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied those mendicants. They did as the Buddha asked, then returned to the Buddha

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: and said,

segs.p: “daḍḍhaṁ, bhante, bāhiyassa dārucīriyassa sarīraṁ, thūpo cassa kato.
segs.e: “Sir, Bāhiya’s corpse has been cremated and a monument built for him.
Where has he been reborn in his next life?”

segs.p: “Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, bāhiyo dārucīriyo paccapādi dhammassānudhammaṁ; na ca maṁ dhammādhikaraṇaṁ vihesesi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, Bāhiya was astute. He practiced in line with the teaching, and did not trouble me about the teachings.
Bāhiya of the Bark Cloth has become fully quenched.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Where water and earth,
fire and air have no footing—
there no star does shine,
nor does the sun shed its light;
there the moon glows not,
yet no darkness is found.
And when a sage, a brahmin, finds understanding
through their own sagacity,
then, from forms and formless,
from pleasure and pain they are released.”

segs.p: Ayampi udāno vutto bhagavatā iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a heartfelt saying that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Heartfelt Sayings 2.1
With Mucalinda
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre mucalindamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the Mucalinda tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sattāhaṁ ekapallaṅkena nisinno hoti vimuttisukhapaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: There the Buddha sat cross-legged for seven days without moving, experiencing the bliss of freedom.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena mahā akālamegho udapādi sattāhavaddalikā sītavātaduddinī.
segs.e: Just then a large storm blew up out of season, bringing seven days of precipitation, with cold winds and overcast skies.

segs.p: Atha kho mucalindo nāgarājā sakabhavanā nikkhamitvā bhagavato kāyaṁ sattakkhattuṁ bhogehi parikkhipitvā uparimuddhani mahantaṁ phaṇaṁ vihacca aṭṭhāsi:
segs.e: Mucalinda, the dragon king, came out from his abode, encircled the Buddha’s body with seven coils and spread his large hood over his head, thinking,

segs.p: “mā bhagavantaṁ sītaṁ, mā bhagavantaṁ uṇhaṁ, mā bhagavantaṁ ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphasso”ti.
segs.e: “May the Buddha not be hot or cold, nor be bothered by flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, or reptiles.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: When seven days had passed, the Buddha emerged from that state of immersion.

segs.p: Atha kho mucalindo nāgarājā viddhaṁ vigatavalāhakaṁ devaṁ viditvā bhagavato kāyā bhoge viniveṭhetvā sakavaṇṇaṁ paṭisaṁharitvā māṇavakavaṇṇaṁ abhinimminitvā bhagavato purato aṭṭhāsi pañjaliko bhagavantaṁ namassamāno.
segs.e: When he knew the heavens were clear and cloudless, Mucalinda unwrapped his coils from the Buddha’s body. Hiding his own form, he manifested in the form of a brahmin youth. He stood in front of the Buddha, venerating him with cupped palms.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Seclusion is happiness for the contented
who see the teaching they have learned.
Kindness for the world is happiness
for one who’d not harm a living creature.
Dispassion for the world is happiness
for one who has gone beyond sensual pleasures.
But dispelling the conceit ‘I am’
is truly the ultimate happiness.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.2
Kings
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ upaṭṭhānasālāyaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time, after the meal, on return from almsround, several mendicants sat together in the assembly hall and this discussion came up among them:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, āvuso, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ rājūnaṁ mahaddhanataro vā mahābhogataro vā mahākosataro vā mahāvijitataro vā mahāvāhanataro vā mahabbalataro vā mahiddhikataro vā mahānubhāvataro vā rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro, rājā vā pasenadi kosalo”ti?
segs.e: “Which of these two kings has greater wealth, riches, treasury, dominion, vehicles, forces, might, and power: King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha or King Pasenadi of Kosala?”

segs.p: Ayañcarahi tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ antarākathā hoti vippakatā.
segs.e: At that point the conversation among those mendicants was left unfinished.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat, went to the assembly hall, sat down on the seat spread out,
and addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “kāya nuttha, bhikkhave, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā sannipatitā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhante, amhākaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ upaṭṭhānasālāyaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: So the mendicants told him what they had been talking about when the Buddha arrived. The Buddha said,

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho, āvuso, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ rājūnaṁ mahaddhanataro vā mahābhogataro vā mahākosataro vā mahāvijitataro vā mahāvāhanataro vā mahabbalataro vā mahiddhikataro vā mahānubhāvataro vā rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro, rājā vā pasenadi kosalo’ti?
Ayaṁ kho no, bhante, antarākathā vippakatā, atha bhagavā anuppatto”ti.
“Na khvetaṁ, bhikkhave, tumhākaṁ patirūpaṁ kulaputtānaṁ saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitānaṁ yaṁ tumhe evarūpiṁ kathaṁ katheyyātha.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is not appropriate for you gentlemen who have gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness to talk about such things.
When you’re sitting together you should do one of two things:

segs.p: dhammī vā kathā ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo”ti.
segs.e: discuss the teachings or keep noble silence.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Neither the pleasures of the senses,
nor even divine happiness,
is worth even a sixteenth part
of the happiness of craving’s end.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.3
A Stick
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā kumārakā antarā ca sāvatthiṁ antarā ca jetavanaṁ ahiṁ daṇḍena hananti.
segs.e: Now at that time, between Sāvatthī and the Jeta Grove, several boys were hitting a snake with a stick.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā sambahule kumārake antarā ca sāvatthiṁ antarā ca jetavanaṁ ahiṁ daṇḍena hanante.
segs.e: He saw the boys hitting the snake.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Creatures love happiness,
so if you harm them with a stick
in search of your own happiness,
after death you’ll find no happiness.
Creatures love happiness,
so if you don’t harm them with a stick
in search of your own happiness,
after death you will find happiness.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.4
Esteem
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito, lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And he received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Bhikkhusaṅghopi sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito, lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: And the mendicant Saṅgha was also honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Aññatitthiyā pana paribbājakā asakkatā honti agarukatā amānitā apūjitā anapacitā, na lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: But the wanderers who followed other religions were not honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they didn’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bhagavato sakkāraṁ asahamānā bhikkhusaṅghassa ca, gāme ca araññe ca bhikkhū disvā asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesenti.
segs.e: Then those wanderers who followed other religions, unable to bear the esteem of the mendicant Saṅgha, abused, attacked, harassed, and troubled the mendicants in the village and the wilderness.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “etarahi, bhante, bhagavā sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito, lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
Bhikkhusaṅghopi sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito, lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
Aññatitthiyā pana paribbājakā asakkatā agarukatā amānitā apūjitā anapacitā, na lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
Atha kho te, bhante, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bhagavato sakkāraṁ asahamānā bhikkhusaṅghassa ca, gāme ca araññe ca bhikkhū disvā asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesantī”ti.
Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“When struck by pleasure and pain <j>in the village or wilderness,
regard it not as self or alien.
Contacts strike because of attachment;
how would contacts strike one free of attachment?”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.5
A Lay Follower
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro icchānaṅgalako upāsako sāvatthiṁ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain lay follower from Icchānaṅgalaka arrived at Sāvatthī on some business.

segs.p: Atha kho so upāsako sāvatthiyaṁ taṁ karaṇīyaṁ tīretvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Having concluded his business in Sāvatthī he went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho taṁ upāsakaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this to him:

segs.p: “cirassaṁ kho tvaṁ, upāsaka, imaṁ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṁ idhāgamanāyā”ti.
segs.e: “It’s been a long time, lay follower, since you took the opportunity to come here.”

segs.p: “Cirapaṭikāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamitukāmo, api cāhaṁ kehici kehici kiccakaraṇīyehi byāvaṭo. Evāhaṁ nāsakkhiṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti.
segs.e: “For a long time I’ve wanted to come and see the Buddha, but I wasn’t able, being prevented by my many duties and responsibilities.”
segs.s: a certain lay follower from Icchānaṅgalaka arrived

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“One who has nothing is happy indeed,
a learned person who has appraised the teaching.
See how troubled are those with attachments,
a person bound tight to people.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.6
The Pregnant Woman
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa paribbājakassa daharamāṇavikā pajāpati hoti gabbhinī upavijaññā.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain wanderer had a young brahmin wife who was pregnant and about to give birth.

segs.p: Atha kho sā paribbājikā taṁ paribbājakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: She said to him,

segs.p: “gaccha tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, telaṁ āhara, yaṁ me vijātāya bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: “Go, brahmin, bring oil for my delivery.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, so paribbājako taṁ paribbājikaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The wanderer said,
“But where, my dear, can I get oil?”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho sā paribbājikā taṁ paribbājakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, she said,

segs.p: “gaccha tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, telaṁ āhara, yaṁ me vijātāya bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: “Go, brahmin, bring oil for my delivery.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho so paribbājako taṁ paribbājikaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, the wanderer said,
“But where, my dear, can I get oil?”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho sā paribbājikā taṁ paribbājakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, she said,

segs.p: “gaccha tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, telaṁ āhara, yaṁ me vijātāya bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: “Go, brahmin, bring oil for my delivery.”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa koṭṭhāgāre samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā sappissa vā telassa vā yāvadatthaṁ pātuṁ dīyati, no nīharituṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time ghee and oil were being given away to any ascetic or brahmin at the storehouse of King Pasenadi of Kosala. But it was only to drink there, not to take away.
Knowing this, the wanderer thought,

segs.p: “rañño kho pana pasenadissa kosalassa koṭṭhāgāre samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā sappissa vā telassa vā yāvadatthaṁ pātuṁ dīyati, no nīharituṁ.
Yannūnāhaṁ rañño pasenadissa kosalassa koṭṭhāgāraṁ gantvā telassa yāvadatthaṁ pivitvā gharaṁ āgantvā ucchadditvāna dadeyyaṁ, yaṁ imissā vijātāya bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: “Why don’t I go to the king’s storehouse, drink as much oil as I can, then come home and throw it up so it can be used for the delivery?”

segs.p: Atha kho so paribbājako rañño pasenadissa kosalassa koṭṭhāgāraṁ gantvā telassa yāvadatthaṁ pivitvā gharaṁ āgantvā neva sakkoti uddhaṁ kātuṁ, na pana adho.
segs.e: Then he did just that. But when he got home he was unable to either bring it up or pass it out.

segs.p: So dukkhāhi tibbāhi kharāhi kaṭukāhi vedanāhi phuṭṭho āvaṭṭati parivaṭṭati.
segs.e: He rolled to and fro, suffering painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā taṁ paribbājakaṁ dukkhāhi tibbāhi kharāhi kaṭukāhi vedanāhi phuṭṭhaṁ āvaṭṭamānaṁ parivaṭṭamānaṁ.
segs.e: He saw the wanderer in agony.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Oh! How happy are those with nothing!
Hence knowledge masters are people with nothing.
See how troubled are those with attachments,
a person bound tight to people.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.7
An Only Son
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa upāsakassa ekaputtako piyo manāpo kālaṅkato hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain lay follower’s dear and beloved only child passed away.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā upāsakā allavatthā allakesā divā divassa yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te upāsake bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the middle of the day several lay followers with wet clothes and hair went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho tumhe, upāsakā, allavatthā allakesā idhūpasaṅkamantā divā divassā”ti?
segs.e: “Why, lay followers, have you come here in the middle of the day with wet clothes and hair?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, so upāsako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The lay follower replied,

segs.p: “mayhaṁ kho, bhante, ekaputtako piyo manāpo kālaṅkato.
segs.e: “Sir, my dear and beloved only child has passed away.

segs.p: Tena mayaṁ allavatthā allakesā idhūpasaṅkamantā divā divassā”ti.
segs.e: That’s why we came here in the middle of the day with wet clothes and hair.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Hosts of gods and most human beings are bound
to what seems dear and pleasant.
Gloomy and exhausted,
they fall under the sway of the King of Death.

segs.p: Ye ve divā ca ratto ca,
segs.e: The diligent, who day and night
give up what seems pleasant,
dig out the root of gloom—
Death’s bait so hard to escape.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.8
Suppavāsā
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kuṇḍikāyaṁ viharati kuṇḍadhānavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kuṇḍiyā in the Kuṇḍadhāna Grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena suppavāsā koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāreti.
segs.e: Now at that time Suppavāsā the Koliyan had been pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days.

segs.p: Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā dukkhāhi tibbāhi kharāhi kaṭukāhi vedanāhi phuṭṭhā tīhi vitakkehi adhivāseti:
segs.e: While suffering painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings, three thoughts helped her endure:

segs.p: “sammāsambuddho vata so bhagavā yo imassa evarūpassa dukkhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti;
segs.e: “Oh! The Blessed One is indeed a fully awakened Buddha, who teaches the Dhamma for giving up suffering such as this.

segs.p: suppaṭipanno vata tassa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho yo imassa evarūpassa dukkhassa pahānāya paṭipanno;
segs.e: Oh! The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is indeed practicing well, who practice for giving up suffering such as this.

segs.p: susukhaṁ vata taṁ nibbānaṁ yatthidaṁ evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ na saṁvijjatī”ti.
segs.e: Oh! Extinguishment is so very blissful, where such suffering as this is not found.”

segs.p: Atha kho suppavāsā koliyadhītā sāmikaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then Suppavāsā addressed her husband,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, ayyaputta, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi; appābādhaṁ appātaṅkaṁ lahuṭṭhānaṁ balaṁ phāsuvihāraṁ puccha:
segs.e: “Please, master, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Ask him if he is healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

segs.p: ‘suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati; appābādhaṁ appātaṅkaṁ lahuṭṭhānaṁ balaṁ phāsuvihāraṁ pucchatī’ti.

segs.e: And then say:

segs.p: ‘suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāreti.
segs.e: ‘Suppavāsā the Koliyan has been pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days.

segs.p: Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā dukkhāhi tibbāhi kharāhi kaṭukāhi vedanāhi phuṭṭhā tīhi vitakkehi adhivāseti—
segs.e: While suffering painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings, three thoughts help her endure:

segs.p: sammāsambuddho vata so bhagavā yo imassa evarūpassa dukkhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti;
segs.e: “Oh! The Blessed One is indeed a fully awakened Buddha, who teaches the Dhamma for giving up suffering such as this.

segs.p: suppaṭipanno vata tassa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho yo imassa evarūpassa dukkhassa pahānāya paṭipanno;
segs.e: Oh! The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is indeed practicing well, who practice for giving up suffering such as this.

segs.p: susukhaṁ vata taṁ nibbānaṁ yatthidaṁ evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ na saṁvijjatī’”ti.
segs.e: Oh! Extinguishment is so very blissful, where such suffering as this is not found.”’”

segs.p: “Paraman”ti kho so koliyaputto suppavāsāya koliyadhītāya paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: “Excellent idea,” he replied. He went to the Buddha and told him of his wife’s struggles. The Buddha said:

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho koliyaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
“suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṁ appātaṅkaṁ lahuṭṭhānaṁ balaṁ phāsuvihāraṁ pucchati;
‘suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāreti.
Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā dukkhāhi tibbāhi kharāhi kaṭukāhi vedanāhi phuṭṭhā tīhi vitakkehi adhivāseti—
sammāsambuddho vata so bhagavā yo imassa evarūpassa dukkhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti;
suppaṭipanno vata tassa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho yo imassa evarūpassa dukkhassa pahānāya paṭipanno;
susukhaṁ vata nibbānaṁ yatthidaṁ evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ na saṁvijjatī’”ti.
“Sukhinī hotu suppavāsā koliyadhītā; arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijāyatū”ti.
segs.e: “May Suppavāsā the Koliyan be happy and healthy! May she give birth to a healthy child!”

segs.p: Saha vacanā ca pana bhagavato suppavāsā koliyadhītā sukhinī arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijāyi.
segs.e: As soon as he spoke, Suppavāsā, happy and healthy, gave birth to a healthy child.

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so koliyaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yena sakaṁ gharaṁ tena paccāyāsi.
segs.e: Saying “Yes, sir,” the Koliyan gentleman approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he returned to his own house.

segs.p: Addasā kho so koliyaputto suppavāsaṁ koliyadhītaraṁ sukhiniṁ arogaṁ arogaṁ puttaṁ vijātaṁ.
segs.e: He saw that his wife, happy and healthy, had given birth to a healthy child,
and thought,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāmāyaṁ suppavāsā koliyadhītā saha vacanā ca pana bhagavato sukhinī arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijāyissatī”ti.
segs.e: “Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! The Realized One has such psychic power and might! For as soon as he spoke, Suppavāsā, happy and healthy, gave birth to a healthy child.”
He became uplifted and overjoyed, full of rapture and happiness.

segs.p: Atha kho suppavāsā koliyadhītā sāmikaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then Suppavāsā addressed her husband,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, ayyaputta, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi:
segs.e: “Please, master, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet.

segs.p: ‘suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti;

segs.e: And then say,

segs.p: ‘suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāreti.
segs.e: ‘Suppavāsā the Koliyan, who was pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days,

segs.p: Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā etarahi sukhinī arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijātā.
segs.e: is now happy and healthy and has given birth to a healthy child.

segs.p: Sā sattāhaṁ buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhattena nimanteti.
segs.e: She invites the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha to a meal for seven days.

segs.p: Adhivāsetu kira, bhante, bhagavā suppavāsāya koliyadhītāya satta bhattāni saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghenā’”ti.
segs.e: Sir, would the Buddha please accept seven meals from Suppavāsā?’”

segs.p: “Paraman”ti kho so koliyaputto suppavāsāya koliyadhītāya paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: “Excellent idea,” he replied. He went to the Buddha, told him the good news, and conveyed his wife’s invitation.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so koliyaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
“Suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati;
‘suppavāsā, bhante, koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāreti.
Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā etarahi sukhinī arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijātā.
Sā sattāhaṁ buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhattena nimanteti.
Adhivāsetu kira, bhante, bhagavā suppavāsāya koliyadhītāya satta bhattāni saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghenā’”ti.
Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena upāsakena buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho svātanāya bhattena nimantito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain lay follower had already invited the Saṅgha of monks headed by the Buddha for the meal on the following day.

segs.p: So ca upāsako āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa upaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: That lay follower was Venerable Mahāmoggallāna’s supporter.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha addressed Venerable Mahāmoggallāna,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, moggallāna, yena so upāsako tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ upāsakaṁ evaṁ vadehi:
segs.e: “Please, Moggallāna, go to that lay follower and say to him,

segs.p: ‘suppavāsā, āvuso, koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāresi.
segs.e: ‘Suppavāsā the Koliyan, who was pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days,

segs.p: Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā etarahi sukhinī arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijātā.
segs.e: is now happy and healthy and has given birth to a healthy child.

segs.p: Sā sattāhaṁ buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhattena nimanteti.
segs.e: She invites the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha to a meal for seven days.

segs.p: Karotu suppavāsā koliyadhītā satta bhattāni, pacchā tvaṁ karissasī’ti.
segs.e: Let Suppavāsā make seven meals, afterwards you can make yours.’
He is your supporter.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavato paṭissutvā yena so upāsako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ upāsakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Mahāmoggallāna. He went to that lay follower and conveyed the Buddha’s request.

segs.p: “suppavāsā, āvuso, koliyadhītā satta vassāni gabbhaṁ dhāreti.
Sattāhaṁ mūḷhagabbhā sā etarahi sukhinī arogā arogaṁ puttaṁ vijātā.
Sā sattāhaṁ buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhattena nimanteti.
Karotu suppavāsā koliyadhītā satta bhattāni, pacchā tvaṁ karissasī”ti.
“Sace me, bhante, ayyo mahāmoggallāno tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pāṭibhogo—
segs.e: “If, sir, Master Mahāmoggallāna can guarantee me three things—
wealth, life, and faith—

segs.p: karotu suppavāsā koliyadhītā satta bhattāni, pacchāhaṁ karissāmī”ti.
segs.e: then let Suppavāsā make seven meals, afterwards I shall make mine.”

segs.p: “Dvinnaṁ kho te ahaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ pāṭibhogo—
segs.e: “I can guarantee you two things—
wealth and life.
But as for faith, you alone are the guarantor.”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, ayyo mahāmoggallāno dvinnaṁ dhammānaṁ pāṭibhogo—
segs.e: “If, sir Master Mahāmoggallāna can guarantee me two things—
wealth and life—

segs.p: karotu suppavāsā koliyadhītā satta bhattāni, pacchāhaṁ karissāmī”ti.
segs.e: then let Suppavāsā make seven meals, afterwards I shall make mine.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ upāsakaṁ saññāpetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Having persuaded that lay follower, Mahāmoggallāna went to the Buddha and said,
“I’ve persuaded the lay follower.

segs.p: karotu suppavāsā koliyadhītā satta bhattāni, pacchā so karissatī”ti.
segs.e: Let Suppavāsā make seven meals, afterwards he shall make his.”

segs.p: Atha kho suppavāsā koliyadhītā sattāhaṁ buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi,
segs.e: For seven days Suppavāsā served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with her own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: tañca dārakaṁ bhagavantaṁ vandāpesi sabbañca bhikkhusaṅghaṁ.
segs.e: And she made her little boy bow to the Buddha and the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto taṁ dārakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāriputta said to the boy,

segs.p: “kacci te, dāraka, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci na kiñci dukkhan”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, little boy, I hope you’re all right. I hope you are not in pain.”

segs.p: “Kuto me, bhante sāriputta, khamanīyaṁ, kuto yāpanīyaṁ.
segs.e: “How could I be keeping well? How could I be getting by?
For seven years I lived in a pot of blood.”
Then Suppavāsā, thinking,

segs.p: “putto me dhammasenāpatinā saddhiṁ mantetī”ti attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā ahosi.
segs.e: “My child is conversing with the General of the Dhamma!” was uplifted and overjoyed, full of rapture and happiness.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā suppavāsaṁ koliyadhītaraṁ attamanaṁ pamuditaṁ pītisomanassajātaṁ viditvā suppavāsaṁ koliyadhītaraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Knowing this, the Buddha said to her,
“Would you like to have another child like this?”
“Sir, I would like to have seven more children like this!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Pain in the guise of pleasure,
the disliked in the guise of the liked,
suffering in the guise of happiness,
overpower the negligent.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.9
With Visākhā
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena visākhāya migāramātuyā kocideva attho raññe pasenadimhi kosale paṭibaddho hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Visākhā was caught up in some business with King Pasenadi.

segs.p: Taṁ rājā pasenadi kosalo na yathādhippāyaṁ tīreti.
segs.e: But the king’s settlement did not meet her expectations.

segs.p: Atha kho visākhā migāramātā divā divassa yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then, in the middle of the day, she went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho visākhaṁ migāramātaraṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, visākhe, āgacchasi divā divassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Visākhā, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

segs.p: “Idha me, bhante, kocideva attho raññe pasenadimhi kosale paṭibaddho;
segs.e: “Sir, I am caught up in some business with King Pasenadi.

segs.p: taṁ rājā pasenadi kosalo na yathādhippāyaṁ tīretī”ti.
segs.e: But the king’s settlement did not meet my expectations.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“All under another’s control is suffering,
all under one’s own authority is pleasing;
what’s shared is stressful for both parties,
for yokes are hard to escape.”
Heartfelt Sayings 2.10
With Bhaddiya
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā anupiyāyaṁ viharati ambavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Anupiya in a mango grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā bhaddiyo kāḷīgodhāya putto araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Now at that time, Venerable Bhaddiya son of Kāḷīgodhā, even in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, frequently expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!”

segs.p: Assosuṁ kho sambahulā bhikkhū āyasmato bhaddiyassa kāḷīgodhāya puttassa araññagatassapi rukkhamūlagatassapi suññāgāragatassapi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānentassa:
segs.e: Several mendicants heard him
and thought,

segs.p: “nissaṁsayaṁ kho, āvuso, āyasmā bhaddiyo kāḷīgodhāya putto anabhirato brahmacariyaṁ carati,
segs.e: “Without a doubt, Venerable Bhaddiya leads the spiritual life dissatisfied.

segs.p: yaṁsa pubbe agāriyabhūtassa rajjasukhaṁ, so tamanussaramāno araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: It’s when recalling the pleasures of royalty he formerly enjoyed as a layperson that, even in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, he frequently expresses this heartfelt sentiment:
‘Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!’”

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what was happening.

segs.p: “āyasmā, bhante, bhaddiyo kāḷīgodhāya putto araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
Nissaṁsayaṁ kho, bhante, āyasmā bhaddiyo kāḷīgodhāya putto anabhirato brahmacariyaṁ carati.
Yaṁsa pubbe agāriyabhūtassa rajjasukhaṁ, so tamanussaramāno araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena bhaddiyaṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantehi:
segs.e: “Please, monk, in my name tell the mendicant Bhaddiya that
the Teacher summons him.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā bhaddiyo kāḷīgodhāya putto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhaddiyaṁ kāḷīgodhāya puttaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to Bhaddiya and said to him,
“Reverend Bhaddiya, the Teacher summons you.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā bhaddiyo kāḷīgodhāya putto tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ bhaddiyaṁ kāḷīgodhāya puttaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Bhaddiya replied. He went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Saccaṁ kira tvaṁ, bhaddiya, araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: “Is it really true, Bhaddiya, that even in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, you frequently express this heartfelt sentiment:
‘Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!’?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana tvaṁ, bhaddiya, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: “But why do you say this?”

segs.p: “Pubbe me, bhante, agāriyabhūtassa rajjaṁ kārentassa antopi antepure rakkhā susaṁvihitā ahosi, bahipi antepure rakkhā susaṁvihitā ahosi, antopi nagare rakkhā susaṁvihitā ahosi, bahipi nagare rakkhā susaṁvihitā ahosi, antopi janapade rakkhā susaṁvihitā ahosi, bahipi janapade rakkhā susaṁvihitā ahosi.
segs.e: “Formerly, as a layperson ruling the land, my guard was well organized within and without the royal compound, within and without the city, and within and without the country.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, bhante, evaṁ rakkhito gopito santo bhīto ubbiggo ussaṅkī utrāsī vihāsiṁ.
segs.e: But although I was guarded and defended in this way, I remained fearful, scared, suspicious, and nervous.

segs.p: Etarahi kho panāhaṁ, bhante, araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi eko abhīto anubbiggo anussaṅkī anutrāsī appossukko pannalomo paradattavutto, migabhūtena cetasā viharāmi.
segs.e: But these days, even when alone in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, I’m not fearful, scared, suspicious, or nervous. I live relaxed, unruffled, surviving on charity, my heart free as a wild deer.

segs.p: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi abhikkhaṇaṁ udānaṁ udānesiṁ:
segs.e: It is for this reason that, even in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, I frequently expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
‘Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!’”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“They who hide no anger within,
passed beyond any kind of existence;
happy, free from fear and sorrow—
even the gods can’t see them.”
Heartfelt Sayings 3.1
Born of the Fruits of Deeds
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya purāṇakammavipākajaṁ dukkhaṁ tibbaṁ kharaṁ kaṭukaṁ vedanaṁ adhivāsento sato sampajāno avihaññamāno.
segs.e: Now, at that time a certain mendicant was sitting not far from the Buddha, cross-legged, with his body straight. As a result of past deeds, he suffered painful, sharp, severe, and acute feelings, which he endured unbothered, with mindfulness and awareness.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ avidūre nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya purāṇakammavipākajaṁ dukkhaṁ tibbaṁ kharaṁ kaṭukaṁ vedanaṁ adhivāsentaṁ sataṁ sampajānaṁ avihaññamānaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him meditating and enduring that pain.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“A mendicant who has left all deeds behind,
shaking off the dust of past deeds,
unselfish, steady, unaffected,
has no need to complain.”
Heartfelt Sayings 3.2
With Nanda
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nando bhagavato bhātā mātucchāputto sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ evamāroceti:
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Nanda, the Buddha’s brother and maternal cousin, informed several mendicants:
“I lead the spiritual life dissatisfied.

segs.p: na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ, sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī”ti.
segs.e: I am unable to keep up the spiritual life. I shall resign the training and return to a lesser life.”

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what was happening.

segs.p: “āyasmā, bhante, nando bhagavato bhātā mātucchāputto sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ evamāroceti:
‘anabhirato ahaṁ, āvuso, brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ, sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī’”ti.
Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena nandaṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantehi:
segs.e: “Please, monk, in my name tell the mendicant Nanda that
the Teacher summons him.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā nando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ nandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to Nanda and said to him,
“Reverend Nanda, the Teacher summons you.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā nando tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ nandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Nanda replied. He went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Saccaṁ kira tvaṁ, nanda, sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ evamārocesi:
segs.e: “Is it really true, Nanda, that you informed several mendicants that

segs.p: ‘anabhirato ahaṁ, āvuso, brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ, sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī’”ti?
segs.e: you are unable to keep up the spiritual life; that you shall resign the training and return to a lesser life?”
“Yes, sir,” he replied.

segs.p: “Kissa pana tvaṁ, nanda, anabhirato brahmacariyaṁ carasi, na sakkosi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ, sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissasī”ti?
segs.e: “But why are you so dissatisfied with the spiritual life?”

segs.p: “Sākiyānī maṁ, bhante, janapadakalyāṇī gharā nikkhamantassa upaḍḍhullikhitehi kesehi apaloketvā maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “As I left my house, sir, the finest lady of the Sakyan land, her hair half-combed, glanced at me and said,
‘Hurry back, master.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, bhante, tamanussaramāno anabhirato brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ, sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Recalling that, I am dissatisfied and shall resign the training.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nandaṁ bāhāyaṁ gahetvā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ—jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṁsesu pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha took Nanda by the arm and, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the gods of the thirty-three.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena pañcamattāni accharāsatāni sakkassa devānamindassa upaṭṭhānaṁ āgatāni honti kakuṭapādāni.
segs.e: Now at that time five hundred dove-footed nymphs had come to attend to Sakka, the lord of gods.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Nanda,

segs.p: “passasi no tvaṁ, nanda, imāni pañca accharāsatāni kakuṭapādānī”ti?
segs.e: “Nanda, do you see these five hundred dove-footed nymphs?”
“Yes, sir,” he replied.

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, nanda, katamā nu kho abhirūpatarā vā dassanīyatarā vā pāsādikatarā vā, sākiyānī vā janapadakalyāṇī, imāni vā pañca accharāsatāni kakuṭapādānī”ti?
segs.e: “What do you think, Nanda? Who is more attractive, good-looking, and lovely—the finest lady of the Sakyan land, or these five hundred dove-footed nymphs?”
“Compared to these five hundred dove-footed nymphs, the finest lady of the Sakyan land is like a deformed monkey with its ears and nose cut off.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhante, sākiyānī janapadakalyāṇī imesaṁ pañcannaṁ accharāsatānaṁ upanidhāya saṅkhyampi nopeti kalabhāgampi nopeti upanidhimpi nopeti.
segs.e: She doesn’t count, there’s no comparison, she’s not worth a fraction.

segs.p: Atha kho imāni pañca accharāsatāni abhirūpatarāni ceva dassanīyatarāni ca pāsādikatarāni cā”ti.
segs.e: These five hundred dove-footed nymphs are far more attractive, good-looking, and lovely.”
“Rejoice, Nanda, rejoice!

segs.p: Ahaṁ te pāṭibhogo pañcannaṁ accharāsatānaṁ paṭilābhāya kakuṭapādānan”ti.
segs.e: I guarantee you five hundred dove-footed nymphs.”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, bhagavā pāṭibhogo pañcannaṁ accharāsatānaṁ paṭilābhāya kakuṭapādānaṁ, abhiramissāmahaṁ, bhante, bhagavati brahmacariye”ti.
segs.e: “If, sir, you guarantee me five hundred dove-footed nymphs, I shall happily lead the spiritual life under the Buddha.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nandaṁ bāhāyaṁ gahetvā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ—devesu tāvatiṁsesu antarahito jetavane pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha took Nanda by the arm and, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from the gods of the thirty-three and reappeared at Jeta’s Grove.
The mendicants heard,

segs.p: “āyasmā kira nando bhagavato bhātā mātucchāputto accharānaṁ hetu brahmacariyaṁ carati;
segs.e: “It seems Venerable Nanda—who is both the Buddha’s half-brother and maternal cousin—leads the spiritual life for the sake of nymphs.

segs.p: bhagavā kirassa pāṭibhogo pañcannaṁ accharāsatānaṁ paṭilābhāya kakuṭapādānan”ti.
segs.e: And it seems that the Buddha guaranteed him five hundred dove-footed nymphs.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato nandassa sahāyakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ nandaṁ bhatakavādena ca upakkitakavādena ca samudācaranti:
segs.e: Monks who were his friends accused him of being a hireling and a lackey,

segs.p: “bhatako kirāyasmā nando upakkitako kirāyasmā nando accharānaṁ hetu brahmacariyaṁ carati;
segs.e: “It seems Nanda is a hireling, it seems he is a lackey: he leads the spiritual life for the sake of nymphs.

segs.p: bhagavā kirassa pāṭibhogo pañcannaṁ accharāsatānaṁ paṭilābhāya kakuṭapādānan”ti.
segs.e: And it seems that the Buddha guaranteed him five hundred dove-footed nymphs.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā nando sahāyakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bhatakavādena ca upakkitakavādena ca aṭṭīyamāno harāyamāno jigucchamāno eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Nanda—embarrassed, ashamed, and disgusted at being called a hireling and a lackey—living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro kho panāyasmā nando arahataṁ ahosi.
segs.e: Venerable Nanda became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “āyasmā, bhante, nando bhagavato bhātā mātucchāputto āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Venerable Nanda—who is both the Buddha’s half-brother and maternal cousin—has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. He lives having realized it with his own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”
And the knowledge also came to the Buddha:

segs.p: “nando āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.
segs.e: “Nanda has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. He lives having realized it with his own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā nando tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā nando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, Nanda went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “yaṁ me, bhante, bhagavā pāṭibhogo pañcannaṁ accharāsatānaṁ paṭilābhāya kakuṭapādānaṁ, muñcāmahaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ etasmā paṭissavā”ti.
segs.e: “Worthy sir, you guaranteed me five hundred dove-footed nymphs. I release you from that promise.”

segs.p: “Mayāpi kho tvaṁ, nanda, cetasā ceto paricca vidito:
segs.e: “Nanda, I encompassed your mind and knew that

segs.p: ‘nando āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: you had realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom.
And deities also told me about this.

segs.p: ‘āyasmā, bhante, nando bhagavato bhātā mātucchāputto āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
Yadeva kho te, nanda, anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ, athāhaṁ mutto etasmā paṭissavā”ti.
segs.e: As soon as your mind was freed from defilements by not grasping, I was released from that promise.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“The mendicant who has crossed over the bog,
who has crushed the thorn of sensuality,
who has reached the end of delusion,
trembles not at pleasure and pain.”
Heartfelt Sayings 3.3
With Yasoja
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena yasojappamukhāni pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni sāvatthiṁ anuppattāni honti bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: Now at that time five hundred mendicants headed by Yasoja arrived at Sāvatthī to see the Buddha.

segs.p: Tedha kho āgantukā bhikkhū nevāsikehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ paṭisammodamānā senāsanāni paññāpayamānā pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā ahesuṁ.
segs.e: At that, those visiting mendicants, while exchanging pleasantries with the resident mendicants, preparing their lodgings, and putting away their bowls and robes, made a colossal racket.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Ānanda,

segs.p: “ke panete, ānanda, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope”ti?
segs.e: “Ānanda, who’s making that colossal racket? You’d think it was fishermen hauling in a catch!”

segs.p: “Etāni, bhante, yasojappamukhāni pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni sāvatthiṁ anuppattāni bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: “Sir, those five hundred mendicants headed by Yasoja have arrived at Sāvatthī to see the Buddha.

segs.p: Tete āgantukā bhikkhū nevāsikehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ paṭisammodamānā senāsanāni paññāpayamānā pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā”ti.
segs.e: It’s those visiting mendicants who, while exchanging pleasantries with the resident mendicants, preparing their lodgings, and putting away their bowls and robes, made a colossal racket.”
“Well then, Ānanda, in my name tell those mendicants that
the Teacher summons them.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied. He went to those mendicants and said,
“Venerables, the Teacher summons you.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” replied those mendicants. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them,

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu tumhe, bhikkhave, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā, kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, what’s with that colossal racket? You’d think it was fishermen hauling in a catch!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā yasojo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Yasoja said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “imāni, bhante, pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni sāvatthiṁ anuppattāni bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: “Sir, these five hundred mendicants have arrived at Sāvatthī to see the Buddha.

segs.p: Teme āgantukā bhikkhū nevāsikehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ paṭisammodamānā senāsanāni paññāpayamānā pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā”ti.
segs.e: It’s these visiting mendicants who, while exchanging pleasantries with the resident mendicants, preparing their lodgings, and putting away their bowls and robes, made a colossal racket.”

segs.p: “Gacchatha, bhikkhave, paṇāmemi vo; na vo mama santike vatthabban”ti.
segs.e: “Go away, mendicants, I dismiss you. You are not to stay in my presence.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā senāsanaṁ saṁsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena vajjī tena cārikaṁ pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied those mendicants. They got up from their seats, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right. They set their lodgings in order and left, taking their bowls and robes.

segs.p: Vajjīsu anupubbena cārikaṁ caramānā yena vaggumudā nadī tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā vaggumudāya nadiyā tīre paṇṇakuṭiyo karitvā vassaṁ upagacchiṁsu.
segs.e: Traveling stage by stage in the land of the Vajjis, they arrived at the Vaggumudā River. They built leaf huts near the riverbank and there they entered the rainy season.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā yasojo vassūpagato bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then Venerable Yasoja, having entered the rainy season, addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “bhagavatā mayaṁ, āvuso, paṇāmitā atthakāmena hitesinā, anukampakena anukampaṁ upādāya.
segs.e: “Out of sympathy, reverends, the Buddha dismissed us, wanting what’s best for us.

segs.p: Handa mayaṁ, āvuso, tathā vihāraṁ kappema yathā no viharataṁ bhagavā attamano assā”ti.
segs.e: Come, let us live in such a way that the Buddha would be pleased with us.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato yasojassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū vūpakaṭṭhā appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharantā tenevantaravassena sabbeva tisso vijjā sacchākaṁsu.
segs.e: Then those mendicants, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, all realized the three knowledges in that same rainy season.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ yathābhirantaṁ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṁ pakkāmi.
segs.e: When the Buddha had stayed in Sāvatthī as long as he pleased, he set out for Vesālī.

segs.p: Anupubbena cārikaṁ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari.
segs.e: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Vesālī,

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: where he stayed in the hall with the peaked roof.
