The Courtesan
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe dve pūgā aññatarissā gaṇikāya sārattā honti paṭibaddhacittā;
segs.e: Now at that time two gangs were both hopelessly in love with a certain courtesan.

segs.p: bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṁ pāṇīhipi upakkamanti, leḍḍūhipi upakkamanti, daṇḍehipi upakkamanti, satthehipi upakkamanti.
segs.e: Fighting, quarreling, and disputing, they attacked each other with fists, stones, rods, and swords,

segs.p: Te tattha maraṇampi nigacchanti maraṇamattampi dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: resulting in death and deadly pain.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁsu.
segs.e: Then several mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, entered Rājagaha for alms.

segs.p: Rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: Then, after the meal, when they returned from almsround, they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what was happening.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
“Idha, bhante, rājagahe dve pūgā aññatarissā gaṇikāya sārattā paṭibaddhacittā;
bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṁ pāṇīhipi upakkamanti, leḍḍūhipi upakkamanti, daṇḍehipi upakkamanti, satthehipi upakkamanti.
Te tattha maraṇampi nigacchanti maraṇamattampi dukkhan”ti.
Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:

segs.p: “Yañca pattaṁ yañca pattabbaṁ, ubhayametaṁ rajānukiṇṇaṁ, āturassānusikkhato.
segs.e: “What has been attained and what is to be attained are both strewn over with dust for that one training while still sick.

segs.e: Heartfelt Sayings 6.9
Hastening By
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ abbhokāse nisinno hoti telappadīpesu jhāyamānesu.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while oil lamps were burning.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā adhipātakā tesu telappadīpesu āpātaparipātaṁ anayaṁ āpajjanti, byasanaṁ āpajjanti, anayabyasanaṁ āpajjanti.
segs.e: And many moths were falling down and crashing down into the lamps, coming to grief and ruin.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā te sambahule adhipātake tesu telappadīpesu āpātaparipātaṁ anayaṁ āpajjante, byasanaṁ āpajjante, anayabyasanaṁ āpajjante.
segs.e: The Buddha saw the moths coming to grief.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Hastening by, they miss the essence,
sprouting ever more new bonds.
Like moths falling in the flame,
some have become fixed in what is seen or heard.”
Heartfelt Sayings 6.10
Arising
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:

“Yāvakīvañca, bhante, tathāgatā loke nuppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā tāva aññatitthiyā paribbājakā sakkatā honti garukatā mānitā pūjitā apacitā lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: “Sir, so long as the Realized Ones, the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas do not arise in the world, the wanderers of other religions are honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhante, tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā atha aññatitthiyā paribbājakā asakkatā honti agarukatā amānitā apūjitā anapacitā na lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: But when the Realized Ones do arise in the world, the wanderers of other religions are no longer honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they do not receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Bhagavāyeva dāni, bhante, sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ, bhikkhusaṅgho cā”ti.
segs.e: Now only the Buddha is honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And he receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”

segs.p: “Evametaṁ, ānanda, yāvakīvañca, ānanda, tathāgatā loke nuppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā tāva aññatitthiyā paribbājakā sakkatā honti garukatā mānitā pūjitā apacitā lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: “That’s so true, Ānanda. So long as the Realized Ones do not arise in the world, the wanderers of other religions are honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, ānanda, tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā atha aññatitthiyā paribbājakā asakkatā honti agarukatā amānitā apūjitā anapacitā na lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: But when the Realized Ones do arise in the world, the wanderers of other religions are no longer honored in this way.

segs.p: Tathāgatova dāni sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ, bhikkhusaṅgho cā”ti.
segs.e: Now only the Realized One is honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And he receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And so does the mendicant Saṅgha.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“The glow-worm shines so long
as the beacon of the sun does not rise.
But when the dazzling sun has come up,
that light is erased and shines no more.
So too the sophists shine bright
so long as the Buddhas don’t arise in the world.

segs.p: Na takkikā sujjhanti na cāpi sāvakā,
segs.e: The sophists are not purified, nor are their disciples.
Having bad views, they are not freed from suffering.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.1
Bhaddiya the Dwarf (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṁ anekapariyāyena dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Sāriputta was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring Venerable Bhaddiya the Dwarf in many ways with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato lakuṇḍakabhaddiyassa āyasmatā sāriputtena anekapariyāyena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānassa samādapiyamānassa samuttejiyamānassa sampahaṁsiyamānassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucci.
segs.e: Then after being taught like this Bhaddiya’s mind was freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṁ āyasmatā sāriputtena anekapariyāyena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānaṁ samādapiyamānaṁ samuttejiyamānaṁ sampahaṁsiyamānaṁ anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw what had happened.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Above, below, everywhere free,
not contemplating ‘I am this’.
Freed like this, he has crossed the flood
not crossed before, so as to not be reborn.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.2
Bhaddiya the Dwarf (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṁ sekhaṁ maññamāno bhiyyoso mattāya anekapariyāyena dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Sāriputta was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring Venerable Bhaddiya the Dwarf in even more ways with a Dhamma talk, thinking that he was still a trainee.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āyasmantaṁ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṁ sekhaṁ maññamānaṁ bhiyyoso mattāya anekapariyāyena dhammiyā kathāya sandassentaṁ samādapentaṁ samuttejentaṁ sampahaṁsentaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw what was happening.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“They’ve cut the cycle, gone to the wishless;
the streams are dried, they flow no more.
Cut, the cycle no longer spins.
Just this is the end of suffering.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.3
Clinging (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.e: Then several mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.e: Then, after the meal, when they returned from almsround, they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what was happening.

Clinging (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā manussā yebhuyyena kāmesu sattā (…) rattā giddhā gathitā mucchitā ajjhosannā andhīkatā sammattakajātā kāmesu viharanti.
segs.e: Now at that time most of the people in Sāvatthī clung to sensual pleasures. Lustful, greedy, tied, infatuated, attached, and blinded, they lived completely addicted to sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā sāvatthiyā te manusse yebhuyyena kāmesu satte ratte giddhe gathite mucchite ajjhopanne andhīkate sammattakajāte kāmesu viharante.
segs.e: He saw how attached the humans were.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Blinded by sensual pleasures, wrapped in a net,
they are smothered over by craving;
bound by the kinsman of the negligent,
like a fish caught in a funnel-net trap.
They chase old age and death,
like a suckling calf its mother.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.5
Another Discourse with Bhaddiya the Dwarf
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā lakuṇḍakabhaddiyo sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then Venerable Bhaddiya the Dwarf, closely following several mendicants, approached the Buddha.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṁ dūratova sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito āgacchantaṁ dubbaṇṇaṁ duddasikaṁ okoṭimakaṁ yebhuyyena bhikkhūnaṁ paribhūtarūpaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw Venerable Bhaddiya coming off in the distance—ugly, unsightly, deformed, and despised by most of the mendicants.
The Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ bhikkhuṁ dūratova sambahulānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito āgacchantaṁ dubbaṇṇaṁ duddasikaṁ okoṭimakaṁ yebhuyyena bhikkhūnaṁ paribhūtarūpan”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, do you see this monk coming—ugly, unsightly, deformed, and despised by most of the mendicants?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Eso, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo. Na ca sā samāpatti sulabharūpā yā tena bhikkhunā asamāpannapubbā.
segs.e: “That mendicant is very mighty and powerful. It’s not easy to find an attainment that he has not already attained.

segs.p: Yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.
segs.e: And he has realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lives having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“With faultless parts and white canopy,
the one-spoked chariot rolls on.
See it come, untroubled,
with stream cut, unbound.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.6
The Ending of Craving
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā aññāsikoṇḍañño bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṁ paccavekkhamāno.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Koṇḍañña Who Understood was sitting not far from the Buddha, cross-legged, with his body straight, reviewing the freedom through the ending of craving.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ aññāsikoṇḍaññaṁ avidūre nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṁ paccavekkhamānaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him meditating there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“There is no root or ground or leaves for them,
so where would creepers sprout from?
That attentive one is released from bonds:
who is worthy to criticize them?
Even the gods praise them,
and by the Divinity, too, they’re praised.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.7
The Ending of Proliferation
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā attano papañcasaññāsaṅkhāpahānaṁ paccavekkhamāno nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was sitting reviewing his own giving up of the judgments driven by the proliferation of perceptions.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā attano papañcasaññāsaṅkhāpahānaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding his own giving up of the judgments driven by the proliferation of perceptions, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“There is no proliferation remaining in those
who have passed beyond the halter and cross-bar.
The sage who lives without craving
is never scorned by the world with its gods.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.8
Kaccāna
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākaccāno bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya kāyagatāya satiyā ajjhattaṁ parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhitāya.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Mahākaccāna was sitting not far from the Buddha, cross-legged, with his body straight and mindfulness of the body well-established internally on the present.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ avidūre nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya kāyagatāya satiyā ajjhattaṁ parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhitāya.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him meditating there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Their mindfulness would always
be established in the body, constant:

segs.p: No cassa no ca me siyā,
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine,

segs.p: Na bhavissati na ca me bhavissati;
segs.e: It will not be, and it will not be mine.’
Meditating stage by stage on that,
in time they’d cross over clinging.”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.9
The Well
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā mallesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena thūṇaṁ nāma mallānaṁ brāhmaṇagāmo tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Mallas together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a brahmin town of the Mallas named Thūṇa.
The brahmins and householders of Thūṇa heard:

segs.p: “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito mallesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ thūṇaṁ anuppatto”ti.
segs.e: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—while wandering in the land of the Mallas has arrived at Thūṇa, together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.”

segs.p: (…) Udapānaṁ tiṇassa ca bhusassa ca yāva mukhato pūresuṁ:
segs.e: They filled the well with grass and hay right to the top, thinking,
“Don’t let these shavelings, these fake ascetics drink the water.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena rukkhamūlaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: And then the Buddha left the road, went to the root of a tree, and sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: When he was seated he said to Venerable Ānanda:

segs.p: “iṅgha me tvaṁ, ānanda, etamhā udapānā pānīyaṁ āharā”ti.
segs.e: “Go on then, Ānanda, fetch me some water from that well.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “idāni so, bhante, udapāno thūṇeyyakehi brāhmaṇagahapatikehi tiṇassa ca bhusassa ca yāva mukhato pūrito:
segs.e: “Just now, sir, the brahmins and householders of Thūṇa filled the well with grass and hay right to the top, thinking,
‘Don’t let these shavelings, these fake ascetics drink the water.’”
For a second time …

segs.p: tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: For a third time, the Buddha said to Ānanda:

segs.p: “iṅgha me tvaṁ, ānanda, etamhā udapānā pānīyaṁ āharā”ti.
segs.e: “Go on then, Ānanda, fetch me some water from that well.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā pattaṁ gahetvā yena so udapāno tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Ānanda. Taking his bowl he went to the well.

segs.p: Atha kho so udapāno āyasmante ānande upasaṅkamante sabbaṁ taṁ tiṇañca bhusañca mukhato ovamitvā acchassa udakassa anāvilassa vippasannassa yāva mukhato pūrito vissandanto maññe aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: As he approached the well, all the grass and hay erupted out of the well-mouth. The water stood transparent, unclouded, and clear right up to the top, seeming to overflow.
Then Venerable Ānanda thought,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā.
segs.e: “Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! The Realized One has such psychic power and might!

segs.p: Ayañhi so udapāno mayi upasaṅkamante sabbaṁ taṁ tiṇañca bhusañca mukhato ovamitvā acchassa udakassa anāvilassa vippasannassa yāva mukhato pūrito vissandanto maññe ṭhito”ti.
segs.e: For when I approached this well, all the grass and hay erupted out of the well-mouth. The water stood transparent, unclouded, and clear right up to the top, seeming to overflow.”

segs.p: Pattena pānīyaṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Gathering a bowl of drinking water he went back to the Buddha, and said to him,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing! The Realized One has such psychic power and might!

segs.p: Ayañhi so, bhante, udapāno mayi upasaṅkamante sabbaṁ taṁ tiṇañca bhusañca mukhato ovamitvā acchassa udakassa anāvilassa vippasannassa yāva mukhato pūrito vissandanto maññe aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: For when I approached that well, all the grass and hay erupted out of the well-mouth. The water stood transparent, unclouded, and clear right up to the top, seeming to overflow.

segs.p: Pivatu bhagavā pānīyaṁ, pivatu sugato pānīyan”ti.
segs.e: Drink the water, Blessed One! Drink the water, Holy One!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“What difference would a well make
if water is there all the time?
Having cut off craving at the root,
who would go out on a quest?”
Heartfelt Sayings 7.10
King Udena
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena rañño utenassa uyyānagatassa antepuraṁ daḍḍhaṁ hoti, pañca ca itthisatāni kālaṅkatāni honti sāmāvatīpamukhāni.
segs.e: Now at that time, while King Udena was visiting a park, his royal compound burned down. Five hundred women died, with Queen Sāmāvatī at their head.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kosambiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁsu.
segs.e: Then several mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, entered Kosambī for alms.

segs.p: Kosambiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: Then, after the meal, when they returned from almsround, they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him had happened. They asked the Buddha,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
“idha, bhante, rañño utenassa uyyānagatassa antepuraṁ daḍḍhaṁ, pañca ca itthisatāni kālaṅkatāni sāmāvatīpamukhāni.
Tāsaṁ, bhante, upāsikānaṁ kā gati ko abhisamparāyo”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, where have those laywomen been reborn in the next life?”
segs.s: several mendicants robed up in the morning and

segs.p: “Santettha, bhikkhave, upāsikāyo sotāpannā, santi sakadāgāminiyo, santi anāgāminiyo.
segs.e: “Among those laywomen there were stream-enterers, once-returners, and non-returners.

segs.p: Sabbā tā, bhikkhave, upāsikāyo anipphalā kālaṅkatā”ti.
segs.e: None of those laywomen died without some fruit of the practice.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“The world is caught up in delusion,
but is looked on as making sense.
The fool caught up in attachment
is surrounded by darkness.
It seems as if eternal,
but for one who sees, there is nothing.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.1
About Extinguishment (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṁyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk about extinguishment.

segs.p: Tedha bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:

segs.p: “Atthi, bhikkhave, tadāyatanaṁ, yattha neva pathavī, na āpo, na tejo, na vāyo, na ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ, na viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ, na ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ, nāyaṁ loko, na paraloko, na ubho candimasūriyā.
segs.e: “There is, mendicants, that dimension where there is no earth, no water, no fire, no wind; no dimension of infinite space, no dimension of infinite consciousness, no dimension of nothingness, no dimension of neither perception nor non-perception; no this world, no other world, no moon or sun.

segs.p: Tatrāpāhaṁ, bhikkhave, neva āgatiṁ vadāmi, na gatiṁ, na ṭhitiṁ, na cutiṁ, na upapattiṁ;
segs.e: There, mendicants, I say there is no coming or going or remaining or passing away or reappearing.
It is not established, does not proceed, and has no support.
Just this is the end of suffering.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.2
About Extinguishment (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṁyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk about extinguishment.

segs.p: Tedha bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“It’s hard to see what they call the ‘uninclined’,
for the truth is not easy to see.
For one who has penetrated craving,
who knows and sees, there is nothing.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.3
About Extinguishment (3rd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṁyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk about extinguishment.

segs.p: Tedha bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā, manasi katvā, sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā, ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“There is, mendicants, freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.

segs.p: No cetaṁ, bhikkhave, abhavissa ajātaṁ abhūtaṁ akataṁ asaṅkhataṁ, nayidha jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyetha.
segs.e: If there were no freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned, then you would find no escape here from rebirth, from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi ajātaṁ abhūtaṁ akataṁ asaṅkhataṁ, tasmā jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyatī”ti.
segs.e: But since there is freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned, an escape is found from rebirth, from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.4
About Extinguishment (4th)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṁyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk about extinguishment.

segs.p: Tedha bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“For the dependent there is quivering. For the independent there’s no quivering.
When there’s no quivering there is tranquility.
When there is tranquility there’s no inclination.
When there’s no inclination, there’s no coming and going.
When there’s no coming and going, there’s no passing away and reappearing.

segs.p: Cutūpapāte asati nevidha na huraṁ na ubhayamantarena.
segs.e: When there’s no passing away and reappearing there’s no this life or the next or between the two.
Just this is the end of suffering.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.5
With Cunda
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā mallesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena pāvā tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Mallas together with a large Saṅgha when he arrived at Pāvā.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā pāvāyaṁ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane.
segs.e: There he stayed in Cunda the smith’s mango grove.

segs.p: Assosi kho cundo kammāraputto: “bhagavā kira mallesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pāvaṁ anuppatto pāvāyaṁ viharati mayhaṁ ambavane”ti.
segs.e: Cunda heard that the Buddha had arrived and was staying in his mango grove.

segs.p: Atha kho cundo kammāraputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then he went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cundaṁ kammāraputtaṁ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.
segs.e: The Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Atha kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Cunda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṁ saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, would the Buddha, together with the mendicant Saṅgha, please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”
The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Cunda rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho cundo kammāraputto tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ paṭiyādāpetvā pahūtañca sūkaramaddavaṁ bhagavato kālaṁ ārocāpesi:
segs.e: And when the night had passed Cunda had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home, and plenty of pork on the turn. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,
“Sir, it’s time. The meal is ready.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena yena cundassa kammāraputtassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of Cunda together with the mendicant Saṅgha, where he sat down on the seat spread out

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā cundaṁ kammāraputtaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: and addressed Cunda,

segs.p: “yaṁ te, cunda, sūkaramaddavaṁ paṭiyattaṁ tena maṁ parivisa,
segs.e: “Cunda, please serve me with the pork on the turn that you’ve prepared.

segs.p: yaṁ panaññaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ paṭiyattaṁ tena bhikkhusaṅghaṁ parivisā”ti.
segs.e: And serve the mendicant Saṅgha with the other foods.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paṭissutvā yaṁ ahosi sūkaramaddavaṁ paṭiyattaṁ tena bhagavantaṁ parivisi;
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Cunda, and did as he was asked.
segs.s: Cunda, and did as he was asked

segs.p: yaṁ panaññaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ paṭiyattaṁ tena bhikkhusaṅghaṁ parivisi.
Atha kho bhagavā cundaṁ kammāraputtaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha addressed Cunda,

segs.p: “yaṁ te, cunda, sūkaramaddavaṁ avasiṭṭhaṁ taṁ sobbhe nikhaṇāhi.
segs.e: “Cunda, any pork on the turn that’s left over, you should bury it in a pit.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ taṁ, cunda, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yassa taṁ paribhuttaṁ sammā pariṇāmaṁ gaccheyya aññatra tathāgatassā”ti.
segs.e: I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who could properly digest it except the Realized One.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paṭissutvā yaṁ ahosi sūkaramaddavaṁ avasiṭṭhaṁ taṁ sobbhe nikhaṇitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Cunda. He did as he was asked, then came back to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cundaṁ kammāraputtaṁ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk, after which he rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavato cundassa kammāraputtassa bhattaṁ bhuttāvissa kharo ābādho uppajji. Lohitapakkhandikā pabāḷhā vedanā vattanti māraṇantikā.
segs.e: After the Buddha had eaten Cunda’s meal, he fell severely ill with bloody dysentery, struck by dreadful pains, close to death.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāsesi avihaññamāno.
segs.e: But he endured unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Ānanda,
“Come, Ānanda, let’s go to Kusinārā.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.
I’ve heard that after eating
the meal of Cunda the smith,
the attentive one fell severely ill,
with pains, close to death.
A severe sickness struck the Teacher
who had eaten the pork on the turn.
While still purging the Buddha said:
“I’ll go to the citadel of Kusinārā.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṁ rukkhamūlaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha left the road and went to the root of a certain tree, where he addressed Ānanda,

segs.p: “iṅgha me tvaṁ, ānanda, catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññāpehi; kilantosmi, ānanda, nisīdissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Go on then, Ānanda, fold my outer robe in four and spread it out for me. I am tired and will sit down.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññāpesi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Ānanda, and did as he was asked.
segs.s: Ānanda, and did as he was asked

segs.e: The Buddha sat down on the seat spread out,

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: and said to Venerable Ānanda,

segs.p: “iṅgha me tvaṁ, ānanda, pānīyaṁ āhara; pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Go on then, Ānanda, fetch me some water. I am thirsty and will drink.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “idāni, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni. Taṁ cakkacchinnaṁ udakaṁ parittaṁ luḷitaṁ āvilaṁ sandati.
segs.e: “Sir, just now around five hundred carts have passed by. The shallow water has been churned up by their wheels, and it flows cloudy and murky.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhante, kukudhā nadī avidūre acchodakā sātodakā sītodakā setodakā supatitthā ramaṇīyā.
segs.e: The Kakutthā River is not far away, with clear, sweet, cool water, clean, with smooth banks, delightful.

segs.p: Ettha bhagavā pānīyañca pivissati gattāni ca sītīkarissatī”ti.
segs.e: There the Buddha can drink and cool his limbs.”
For a second time …

segs.p: tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: For a third time, the Buddha said to Ānanda,

segs.p: “iṅgha me tvaṁ, ānanda, pānīyaṁ āhara; pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Go on then, Ānanda, fetch me some water. I am thirsty and will drink.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā pattaṁ gahetvā yena sā nadī tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Ānanda. Taking his bowl he went to the river.

segs.p: Atha kho sā nadī cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā āyasmante ānande upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandati.
segs.e: Now, though the shallow water in that river had been churned up by wheels, and flowed cloudy and murky, when Ānanda approached it flowed transparent, clear, and unclouded.
Then Venerable Ānanda thought,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā.
segs.e: “Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! The Realized One has such psychic power and might!

segs.p: Ayañhi sā nadī cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā mayi upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandatī”ti.
segs.e: For though the shallow water in that river had been churned up by wheels, and flowed cloudy and murky, when I approached it flowed transparent, clear, and unclouded.”

segs.p: Pattena pānīyaṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Gathering a bowl of drinking water he went back to the Buddha, and said to him,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing! The Realized One has such psychic power and might!

segs.p: Ayañhi sā, bhante, nadī cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā mayi upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandati.
segs.e: For though the shallow water in that river had been churned up by wheels, and flowed cloudy and murky, when I approached it flowed transparent, clear, and unclouded.

segs.p: Pivatu bhagavā pānīyaṁ, pivatu sugato pānīyan”ti.
segs.e: Drink the water, Blessed One! Drink the water, Holy One!”
So the Buddha drank the water.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena kukudhā nadī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kukudhaṁ nadiṁ ajjhogāhetvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena ambavanaṁ tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants went to the Kakutthā River. He plunged into the river and bathed and drank.
And when he had emerged, he went to the mango grove, where he addressed Venerable Cundaka,

segs.p: “iṅgha me tvaṁ, cundaka, catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññāpehi; kilantosmi, cundaka, nipajjissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Go on then, Cundaka, fold my outer robe in four and spread it out for me. I am tired and will lie down.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā cundako bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññāpesi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Cundaka, and did as he was asked.
segs.s: Cundaka, and did as he was asked

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappesi pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṁ manasi karitvā.
segs.e: And then the Buddha laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up.

segs.p: Āyasmā pana cundako tattheva bhagavato purato nisīdi.
segs.e: But Cundaka sat down right there in front of the Buddha.
Having gone to Kakutthā Creek,
whose water was transparent, sweet, and clear,
the Teacher, being tired, plunged in,
the Realized One, without compare in the world.
And after bathing and drinking the Teacher emerged.
Before the group of mendicants, in the middle, <j>the Buddha,
the Teacher who rolled forth <j>the present dispensation,
the great seer went to the mango grove.
He addressed the mendicant named Cundaka:
“Spread out my folded robe so I can lie down.”
The evolved one urged Cunda,
who quickly spread the folded robe.
The Teacher lay down so tired,
while Cunda sat there before him.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Ānanda,

segs.p: “siyā kho panānanda, cundassa kammāraputtassa koci vippaṭisāraṁ upadaheyya:
segs.e: “Now it may happen, Ānanda, that others may give rise to some regret for Cunda the smith:

segs.p: ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, alābhā, tassa te dulladdhaṁ yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ bhuñjitvā parinibbuto’ti.
segs.e: ‘It’s your loss, respectable Cunda, it’s your misfortune, in that the Realized One was fully quenched after eating his last almsmeal from you.’
You should dispel remorse in Cunda the smith like this:

segs.p: Tassa te, āvuso cunda, lābhā, tassa te suladdhaṁ
segs.e: ‘You’re fortunate, respectable Cunda, you’re so very fortunate,

segs.p: yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto.
segs.e: in that the Realized One was fully quenched after eating his last almsmeal from you.

segs.p: Sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso cunda, bhagavato sutaṁ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
segs.e: I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha.

segs.p: dveme piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā samasamavipākā ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṁsatarā ca.
segs.e: There are two almsmeal offerings that have identical fruit and result, and are more fruitful and beneficial than other almsmeal offerings.
What two?

segs.p: Yañca piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambujjhati, yañca piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjitvā anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati.
segs.e: The almsmeal after eating which a Realized One awakens to the supreme perfect awakening; and the almsmeal after eating which he becomes fully extinguished in the element of extinguishment with no residue.

segs.p: Ime dve piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā samasamavipākā ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṁsatarā ca.
segs.e: These two almsmeal offerings have identical fruit and result, and are more fruitful and beneficial than other almsmeal offerings.

segs.p: ‘Āyusaṁvattanikaṁ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṁ upacitaṁ, vaṇṇasaṁvattanikaṁ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṁ upacitaṁ, sukhasaṁvattanikaṁ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṁ upacitaṁ, saggasaṁvattanikaṁ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṁ upacitaṁ, yasasaṁvattanikaṁ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṁ upacitaṁ, ādhipateyyasaṁvattanikaṁ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṁ upacitan’ti.
segs.e: You’ve accumulated a deed that leads to long life, beauty, happiness, glory, heaven, and sovereignty.’
You should dispel remorse in Cunda the smith like this.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“A giver’s merit grows;
enmity doesn’t build up when you have self-control.
A skillful person gives up bad things—
with the end of greed, hate, and delusion, <j>they’re quenched.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.6
The Layfolk of Pāṭali Village
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā magadhesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena pāṭaligāmo tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Magadhans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at the village of Pāṭali.
The lay followers of Pāṭali Village heard that he had arrived.

segs.p: “bhagavā kira magadhesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pāṭaligāmaṁ anuppatto”ti.
Atha kho pāṭaligāmiyā upāsakā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: So they went to see him, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho pāṭaligāmiyā upāsakā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:

segs.e: “Sir, please consent to come to our guest house.”
The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho pāṭaligāmiyā upāsakā bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yenāvasathāgāraṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā sabbasanthariṁ āvasathāgāraṁ santharitvā āsanāni paññāpetvā udakamaṇikaṁ patiṭṭhāpetvā telappadīpaṁ āropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho pāṭaligāmiyā upāsakā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, the lay followers of Pāṭali Village rose from their seats, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right. Then they went to the guest house, where they spread carpets all over, prepared seats, set up a water jar, and placed an oil lamp. Then they went back to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and told him of their preparations, saying:

segs.p: “sabbasantharisanthataṁ, bhante, āvasathāgāraṁ; āsanāni paññattāni; udakamaṇiko patiṭṭhāpito telappadīpo āropito.

segs.e: “Please, sir, come at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena yena āvasathāgāraṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṁ pavisitvā majjhimaṁ thambhaṁ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi.
segs.e: In the morning, the Buddha robed up and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the guest house together with the Saṅgha of mendicants. Having washed his feet, he entered the guest house and sat against the central column facing east.

segs.p: Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṁ pavisitvā pacchimaṁ bhittiṁ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi bhagavantaṁyeva purakkhatvā.
segs.e: The Saṅgha of mendicants also washed their feet, entered the guest house, and sat against the west wall facing east, with the Buddha right in front of them.

segs.p: Pāṭaligāmiyāpi kho upāsakā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṁ pavisitvā puratthimaṁ bhittiṁ nissāya pacchimābhimukhā nisīdiṁsu bhagavantaṁyeva purakkhatvā.
segs.e: The lay followers of Pāṭali Village also washed their feet, entered the guest house, and sat against the east wall facing west, with the Buddha right in front of them.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmiye upāsake āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha addressed them:
“Householders, there are these five drawbacks for an unethical person because of their failure in ethics.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno pamādādhikaraṇaṁ mahatiṁ bhogajāniṁ nigacchati.
segs.e: Firstly, an unethical person loses great wealth on account of negligence.
This is the first drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person gets a bad reputation.
This is the second drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati—yadi khattiyaparisaṁ, yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ, yadi gahapatiparisaṁ, yadi samaṇaparisaṁ—avisārado upasaṅkamati maṅkubhūto.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person enters any kind of assembly unconfident and embarrassed, whether it’s an assembly of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, or ascetics.
This is the third drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person feels lost when they die.
This is the fourth drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
This is the fifth drawback.

segs.p: Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for an unethical person because of their failure in ethics.
There are these five benefits for an ethical person because of their accomplishment in ethics.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno appamādādhikaraṇaṁ mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ adhigacchati.
segs.e: Firstly, an ethical person gains great wealth on account of diligence.
This is the first benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, sīlavato sīlasampannassa kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an ethical person gets a good reputation.
This is the second benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati—yadi khattiyaparisaṁ, yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ, yadi gahapatiparisaṁ, yadi samaṇaparisaṁ—visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto.
segs.e: Furthermore, an ethical person enters any kind of assembly bold and self-assured, whether it’s an assembly of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, or ascetics.
This is the third benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno asammūḷho kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an ethical person dies not feeling lost.
This is the fourth benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Furthermore, when an ethical person’s body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.
This is the fifth benefit.

segs.p: Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ānisaṁsā sīlavato sīlasampadāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits for an ethical person because of their accomplishment in ethics.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmiye upāsake bahudeva rattiṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uyyojesi:
segs.e: The Buddha spent much of the night educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the lay followers of Pāṭali Village with a Dhamma talk. Then he sent them off,

segs.p: “abhikkantā kho, gahapatayo, ratti; yassadāni tumhe kālaṁ maññathā”ti
segs.e: “The night is getting late, householders. Please go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho pāṭaligāmiyā upāsakā bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: And then the lay followers of Pāṭali Village approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. They got up from their seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu pāṭaligāmiyesu upāsakesu suññāgāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: Soon after they left the Buddha entered a private cubicle.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpenti vajjīnaṁ paṭibāhāya.
segs.e: Now at that time the Magadhan ministers Sunidha and Vassakāra were building a citadel at Pāṭali Village to keep the Vajjis out.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā devatāyo sahassasahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhanti.
segs.e: At that time thousands of deities were taking possession of building sites in Pāṭali Village.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti mahesakkhānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: Illustrious rulers or royal chief ministers inclined to build houses at sites possessed by illustrious deities.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti majjhimānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: Middling rulers or royal chief ministers inclined to build houses at sites possessed by middling deities.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti nīcānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: Lesser rulers or royal chief ministers inclined to build houses at sites possessed by lesser deities.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena tā devatāyo sahassasahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, the Buddha saw those deities taking possession of building sites in Pāṭali Village,

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: and the people building houses in accord with the station of the deities.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
Yasmiṁ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā paccūsasamaye paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: The Buddha rose at the crack of dawn and addressed Ānanda,

segs.p: “Ke nu kho, ānanda, pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpentī”ti.
segs.e: “Ānanda, who is building a citadel at Pāṭali Village?”

segs.p: “Sunidhavassakārā, bhante, magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpenti vajjīnaṁ paṭibāhāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, the Magadhan chief ministers Sunidha and Vassakāra are building a citadel to keep the Vajjis out.”
“It’s as if they were building the citadel in consultation with the gods of the thirty-three.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, ānanda, sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpenti vajjīnaṁ paṭibāhāya.
Idhāhaṁ, ānanda, addasaṁ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sambahulā devatāyo sahassasahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I saw those deities taking possession of building sites.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti mahesakkhānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: Illustrious rulers or royal chief ministers inclined to build houses at sites possessed by illustrious deities.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti majjhimānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: Middling rulers or royal chief ministers inclined to build houses at sites possessed by middling deities.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti nīcānaṁ tattha raññaṁ rājamahāmattānaṁ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṁ.
segs.e: Lesser rulers or royal chief ministers inclined to build houses at sites possessed by lesser deities.

segs.p: Yāvatā, ānanda, ariyaṁ āyatanaṁ yāvatā vaṇippatho idaṁ agganagaraṁ bhavissati pāṭaliputtaṁ puṭabhedanaṁ.
segs.e: As far as the civilized region extends, as far as the trading zone extends, this will be the chief city: the Pāṭaliputta trade center.

segs.p: Pāṭaliputtassa kho, ānanda, tayo antarāyā bhavissanti—
segs.e: But Pāṭaliputta will face three threats:

segs.p: aggito vā udakato vā mithubhedato vā”ti.
segs.e: from fire, flood, and dissension.”

segs.p: Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then the Magadhan ministers Sunidha and Vassakāra approached the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they stood to one side and said,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
“adhivāsetu no bhavaṁ gotamo ajjatanāya bhattaṁ saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti.
segs.e: “Would Worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept today’s meal from me?”

segs.p: Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā yena sako āvasatho tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā sake āvasathe paṇītaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṁ ārocesuṁ:
segs.e: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, they went to their own guest house, where they had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared. Then they had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,
“It’s time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena yena sunidhavassakārānaṁ magadhamahāmattānaṁ āvasatho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to their guest house together with the mendicant Saṅgha, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesuṁ sampavāresuṁ.
segs.e: Then Sunidha and Vassakāra served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ aññataraṁ nīcaṁ āsanaṁ gahetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Sunidha and Vassakāra took a low seat and sat to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi:
segs.e: The Buddha expressed his appreciation with these verses:
“In the place he makes his dwelling,
having fed the astute
and the virtuous here,
the restrained spiritual practitioners,
he should dedicate an offering
to the deities there.
Venerated, they venerate him;
honored, they honor him.
After that they have sympathy for him,
like a mother for the child at her breast.
A man beloved of the deities
always sees nice things.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sunidhavassakārānaṁ magadhamahāmattānaṁ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: When the Buddha had expressed his appreciation to Sunidha and Vassakāra with these verses, he rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti:
segs.e: Sunidha and Vassakāra followed behind the Buddha, thinking,

segs.p: “yenajja samaṇo gotamo dvārena nikkhamissati taṁ gotamadvāraṁ nāma bhavissati.
segs.e: “The gate through which the ascetic Gotama exits today shall be named the Gotama Gate.

segs.p: Yena titthena gaṅgaṁ nadiṁ tarissati taṁ gotamatitthaṁ nāma bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: The ford at which he crosses the Ganges River shall be named the Gotama Ford.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena dvārena nikkhami taṁ gotamadvāraṁ nāma ahosi.
segs.e: Then the gate through which the Buddha exited was named the Gotama Gate.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena gaṅgā nadī tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha came to the Ganges River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena gaṅgā nadī pūrā hoti samatittikā kākapeyyā.
segs.e: Now at that time the Ganges was full to the brim so a crow could drink from it.

segs.p: Appekacce manussā nāvaṁ pariyesanti, appekacce uḷumpaṁ pariyesanti, appekacce kullaṁ bandhanti apārā pāraṁ gantukāmā.
segs.e: Wanting to cross from the near to the far shore, some people were seeking a boat, some a dinghy, while some were tying up a raft.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ—gaṅgāya nadiyā orimatīre antarahito pārimatīre paccuṭṭhāsi saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena.
segs.e: But, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, the Buddha, together with the mendicant Saṅgha, vanished from the near shore and landed on the far shore.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā te manusse appekacce nāvaṁ pariyesante, appekacce uḷumpaṁ pariyesante, appekacce kullaṁ bandhante apārā pāraṁ gantukāme.
segs.e: He saw all those humans wanting to cross over.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Those who cross a deluge or stream
have built a bridge and left the marshes behind.
While some people are still tying a raft,
intelligent people have crossed over.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.7
A Fork in the Road
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti āyasmatā nāgasamālena pacchāsamaṇena.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was traveling along a road in the Kosalan lands with Venerable Nāgasamāla as his second monk.

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā nāgasamālo antarāmagge dvidhāpathaṁ.
segs.e: Nāgasamāla saw a fork in the road
and said to the Buddha,
“Sir, this is the road,
let us go this way.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nāgasamālaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: But when he said this the Buddha responded,
“Nāgasamāla, this is the road,
let us go this way.”
For a second time …

segs.p: tatiyampi kho āyasmā nāgasamālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time Nāgasamāla said to the Buddha,
“Sir, this is the road,
let us go this way.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nāgasamālaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time the Buddha responded,
“Nāgasamāla, this is the road,
let us go this way.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā nāgasamālo bhagavato pattacīvaraṁ tattheva chamāyaṁ nikkhipitvā pakkāmi:
segs.e: Then Nāgasamāla put the Buddha’s bowl and robes down on the ground right there and left, saying,
“Sir, here are your bowl and robes.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato nāgasamālassa tena panthena gacchantassa antarāmagge corā nikkhamitvā hatthehi ca pādehi ca ākoṭesuṁ pattañca bhindiṁsu saṅghāṭiñca vipphālesuṁ.
segs.e: Then as Nāgasamāla was going down that road, he was set upon by bandits who struck him with fists and feet, broke his bowl, and tore up his outer robe.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā nāgasamālo bhinnena pattena vipphālitāya saṅghāṭiyā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Nāgasamāla—with his bowl broken and his outer robe torn—went to the Buddha and told him what had happened.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā nāgasamālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
“idha mayhaṁ, bhante, tena panthena gacchantassa antarāmagge corā nikkhamitvā hatthehi ca pādehi ca ākoṭesuṁ, pattañca bhindiṁsu, saṅghāṭiñca vipphālesun”ti.
Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Walking together, dwelling as one,
the knowledge master mixes with foolish folk.
Knowing this, they give up wickedness,
like a milk-drinking heron the water.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.8
With Visākhā
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena visākhāya migāramātuyā nattā kālaṅkatā hoti piyā manāpā.
segs.e: Now at that time the dear and beloved granddaughter of Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, had just passed away.

segs.p: Atha kho visākhā migāramātā allavatthā allakesā divā divassa yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then, in the middle of the day, Visākhā with wet clothes and hair went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho visākhaṁ migāramātaraṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to her,

segs.p: “Handa kuto nu tvaṁ, visākhe, āgacchasi allavatthā allakesā idhūpasaṅkantā divā divassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Visākhā, where are you coming from in the middle of the day with wet clothes and hair?”
“Sir, my beloved granddaughter has just passed away.

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ allavatthā allakesā idhūpasaṅkantā divā divassā”ti.
segs.e: That’s why I came here in the middle of the day with wet clothes and hair.”

segs.p: “Iccheyyāsi tvaṁ, visākhe, yāvatikā sāvatthiyā manussā tāvatike putte ca nattāro cā”ti?
segs.e: “Visākhā, would you like as many children and grandchildren as there are people in the whole of Sāvatthī?”

segs.p: “Iccheyyāhaṁ, bhagavā, yāvatikā sāvatthiyā manussā tāvatike putte ca nattāro cā”ti.
segs.e: “I would, sir.”

segs.p: “Kīvabahukā pana, visākhe, sāvatthiyā manussā devasikaṁ kālaṁ karontī”ti?
segs.e: “But Visākhā, how many people pass away each day in Sāvatthī?”

segs.p: “Dasapi, bhante, sāvatthiyā manussā devasikaṁ kālaṁ karonti;
segs.e: “Every day, sir, there are ten people passing away in Sāvatthī.
Or else there are nine,
eight,
seven,
six,
five,
four,
three,

segs.p: dvepi, bhante, sāvatthiyā manussā devasikaṁ kālaṁ karonti.
segs.e: two,

segs.p: Ekopi, bhante, sāvatthiyā manusso devasikaṁ kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: or at least one person who passes away every day in Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Avivittā, bhante, sāvatthi manussehi kālaṁ karontehī”ti.
segs.e: Sāvatthī is never without someone passing away.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, visākhe, api nu tvaṁ kadāci karahaci anallavatthā vā bhaveyyāsi anallakesā vā”ti?
segs.e: “What do you think, Visākhā? Would there ever be a time when your clothes and hair were not wet?”
“No, sir.

segs.p: Alaṁ me, bhante, tāva bahukehi puttehi ca nattārehi cā”ti.
segs.e: Enough, sir, with so many children and grandchildren.”

segs.p: “Yesaṁ kho, visākhe, sataṁ piyāni, sataṁ tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: “Those who have a hundred loved ones, Visākhā, have a hundred sufferings.

segs.p: yesaṁ navuti piyāni, navuti tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: Those who have ninety loved ones,

segs.p: yesaṁ asīti piyāni, asīti tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: or eighty,

segs.p: yesaṁ sattati piyāni, sattati tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: seventy,

segs.p: yesaṁ saṭṭhi piyāni, saṭṭhi tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: sixty,

segs.p: yesaṁ paññāsaṁ piyāni, paññāsaṁ tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: fifty,

segs.p: yesaṁ cattārīsaṁ piyāni, cattārīsaṁ tesaṁ dukkhāni,
segs.e: forty,

segs.p: yesaṁ tiṁsaṁ piyāni, tiṁsaṁ tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: thirty,

segs.p: yesaṁ vīsati piyāni, vīsati tesaṁ dukkhāni,
segs.e: twenty,

segs.p: yesaṁ dasa piyāni, dasa tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: ten,

segs.p: yesaṁ nava piyāni, nava tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: nine,

segs.p: yesaṁ aṭṭha piyāni, aṭṭha tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: eight,

segs.p: yesaṁ satta piyāni, satta tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: seven,

segs.p: yesaṁ cha piyāni, cha tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: six,

segs.p: yesaṁ pañca piyāni, pañca tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: five,

segs.p: yesaṁ cattāri piyāni, cattāri tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: four,

segs.p: yesaṁ tīṇi piyāni, tīṇi tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: three,

segs.p: yesaṁ dve piyāni, dve tesaṁ dukkhāni;
segs.e: two,

segs.p: yesaṁ ekaṁ piyaṁ, ekaṁ tesaṁ dukkhaṁ;
segs.e: or one loved one have one suffering.

segs.p: yesaṁ natthi piyaṁ, natthi tesaṁ dukkhaṁ, asokā te virajā anupāyāsāti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: Those who have no loved ones have no suffering. They are free of sorrow, stains, and anguish I say.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“All the sorrows and lamentations
and the countless forms of suffering in the world
occur because of those that we love;
without loved ones they do not occur.
That’s why those who have no loved ones <j>at all in the world
are happy and free of grief.
So aspiring to the sorrowless and stainless,
have no loved ones in the world at all.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.9
With Dabba (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Dabba the Mallian went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:

segs.e: “Holy One, it is the time for my full extinguishment.”
“Please, Dabba, do as you see fit.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā vehāsaṁ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhahitvā parinibbāyi.
segs.e: Then Dabba rose from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he rose into the air and, sitting cross-legged in midair, entered and withdrew from the fire element before becoming fully extinguished.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa vehāsaṁ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhahitvā parinibbutassa sarīrassa jhāyamānassa ḍayhamānassa neva chārikā paññāyittha na masi.
segs.e: Then when he was fully quenched while sitting cross-legged in midair, his body burning and combusting left neither ashes nor soot to be found.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma sappissa vā telassa vā jhāyamānassa ḍayhamānassa neva chārikā paññāyati na masi;
segs.e: It’s like when ghee or oil blaze and burn, and neither ashes nor soot are found.

segs.p: evamevaṁ āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa vehāsaṁ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhahitvā parinibbutassa sarīrassa jhāyamānassa ḍayhamānassa neva chārikā paññāyittha na masīti.
Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“The body is broken up, perception has ceased,
all feelings have become cool;
choices are stilled,
and consciousness come to an end.”
Heartfelt Sayings 8.10
Dabba (2nd)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Dabbassa, bhikkhave, mallaputtassa vehāsaṁ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhahitvā parinibbutassa sarīrassa jhāyamānassa ḍayhamānassa neva chārikā paññāyittha na masi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when Dabba the Mallian rose into the air and, sitting cross-legged in midair, entered and withdrew from the fire element before becoming fully quenched, his body burning and combusting left neither ashes nor soot to be found.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma sappissa vā telassa vā jhāyamānassa ḍayhamānassa neva chārikā paññāyati na masi;
segs.e: It’s like when ghee or oil blaze and burn, and neither ashes nor soot are found.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dabbassa mallaputtassa vehāsaṁ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhahitvā parinibbutassa sarīrassa jhāyamānassa ḍayhamānassa neva chārikā paññāyittha na masī”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, when Dabba the Mallian rose into the air and, sitting cross-legged in midair, entered and withdrew from the fire element before becoming fully quenched, his body burning and combusting left neither ashes nor soot to be found.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:
“Just as the glow of iron struck
by a hammer in the fire of Jātaveda
gradually dissipates,
its destiny unknown;
in the same way, for the rightly released,
who have crossed the flood of sensual bonds,
there is no destination to describe—
they have found unshakable happiness.”
The Heartfelt Sayings are finished.
